items.summary: An intellectual property tribunal ruled that OpenAI failed to stop a Singapore start-up from registering the name “GemGPT”. Principal assistant registrar Gabriel Ong found sharing the letters GPT was not enough, as ChatGPT and GemGPT were whole names. Porolis Technologies can proceed with its trademark for AI-powered gemstone services and was awarded $10,000 in costs. OpenAI’s five objections were rejected.
items.title: OpenAI Loses Bid to Block GemGPT Trademark in Singapore

items.summary: NVIDIA and its partners are expanding physical AI, agentic AI and local AI factories for cities worldwide, building on initiatives announced at GTC Berlin. Shared computing infrastructure gives city departments, neighboring municipalities and developers a common foundation to build services without each organization managing resources of its own. Partners include ITMAX in Malaysia, scaling SamurAI V2 vision agents across 17,000+ cameras by 2027; Barcelona Supercomputing Center’s AI Factory Accelerator Programme for startups; and Linker Vision with MVRDV in Taiwan, whose environmental agents simulate a 15-year urban forest canopy in 10 minutes. Details are to be shared at Smart City Expo World Congress in Barcelona Nov. 3-5, where NVIDIA Vice President of EMEA Paolo Guglielmini will deliver a keynote followed by a panel moderated by Charbel Aoun. The event runs Nov.
items.title: NVIDIA Expands Physical and Agentic AI Across Cities Worldwide

items.summary: Apple is rolling out its AI-powered “Audio Intelligence” technology for the Apple Watch into beta testing, initially reaching developers in the iOS 27.3 update after being announced at the company’s Surprise and Shine hardware event in September. The set of four opt-in features lets Series 12 wearers detect important sounds, identify songs via Shazam, catch up on conversations through Live Rewind, and take notes with Siri Recaps. Apple emphasizes privacy safeguards, including not identifying speakers or saving raw audio, automatic deletion of unsaved snippets after 30 seconds, and secure processing that excludes even the company from accessing recorded content.
items.title: Apple Watch Audio Intelligence Features Enter Beta Testing

items.summary: Singapore Exchange Regulation (SGX RegCo) announced on Nov 3 that it will fully manage the listing review process from Jan 4, 2027, committing to complete applications within six to eight weeks. The change follows a month-long consultation and aims to streamline submissions through a single electronic portal while MAS retains oversight of disclosure exemptions.
items.title: SGX RegCo Takes Over Listing Review To Speed Up Process

items.summary: PyTorchKR and XCENA co-hosted KVCache Meetup Korea on Sep 30, 2026. Speakers from XCENA, SK hynix, FuriosaAI, and LMCache presented technical talks covering CXL memory expansion, GPU compute and HBM bandwidth bottlenecks, request scheduling for RNGD inference engines, and LMCache's multi-platform cache management layer. Sessions included a Roofline analysis using two H100 GPUs with Llama 3.1 8B on vLLM, where retrieving host cache took about 92 ms versus recomputing at about 900 ms under a 12,370-token prompt. Feedback from 72 survey responses showed the program received 48 positive selections (66.7%), with requests for real production examples and translation support noted by organizers planning future events.
items.title: KVCache Meetup Korea Recap Draws AI Inference Feedback

items.summary: OpenAI has introduced Pando, a new Git-compatible server backend that now serves all development in its monorepo while keeping the standard Git client and protocol. The team reports median push latency fell nearly 80%, roughly five times faster, with daily traffic near one petabyte of Git data. OpenAI built Pando in Rust over about 10 weeks; one engineer designed the core and Codex agents implemented it. It reached production in April 2026 after pushes and fetches slowed by late 2025. All performance figures are self-reported, with no independent benchmark yet, and Pando is not open source.
items.title: OpenAI Ships Pando, a Git Backend That Cuts Push Latency ~80%

items.summary: On July 30, 2026, the Transformers library enabled PyTorch's scaled dot-product attention (SDPA) for T5. As a side effect, UMT5's decoder could attend to future tokens during training and peek at answers it was supposed to predict. The bug stayed in main for almost two months before being fixed on September 28. To catch such regressions earlier, the team introduced Model Integration Contracts (MICs): published small fixtures built from real checkpoints that run fast integration tests on cheap CPU runners against recorded baselines. A UMT5 fixture flagged the regression across five months of commits; its runner step took 13.4 seconds on CPU. The approach is still being evaluated, as reported failures do not block PRs and coverage remains partial.
items.title: Hugging Face Adds Model Integration Contracts for Transformers Models

items.summary: In an opinion piece dated Nov 2, 2026, Maria Federica Martino Lena argues the European Commission’s new AI Office can expose the judgment calls behind frontier labs’ safety claims without needing more power. Since Aug. 2, 2026, the Office may enforce general-purpose AI obligations under Articles 91, 92 and 93 of the AI Act. Yet she says it enforces against definitions it cannot easily control or compare, because providers still set what “frontier,” “safe” and conclusive evaluation mean. She proposes a regulator-owned public taxonomy that records where value-laden choices occur across a model’s lifecycle, making them legible and contestable rather than hidden as technical facts. The piece cites OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra System Card (§10. 1. 1) on counting refusals as successes, its reduced monitorability under §9, and Anthropic withholding pre-release access to Mythos 5. 1 before Dario Amodei’s “We Must Pace the Frontier” (referenced in sentence s34), where a version number of 5.
items.title: EU AI Office Could Make Frontier Labs’ Safety Judgments Visible

items.summary: Huawei Digital Power, Huawei's energy technology unit, notified customers of planned price increases of 5% to 15% across several solar and storage product lines. The company said it had absorbed some extra manufacturing costs but could no longer hold existing prices without risking quality or service. It cited rising commodity, PCB and memory prices since 2025 and did not set an implementation date. Huawei is the latest in a series of Chinese suppliers to raise prices; copper hit $14,700 per metric ton in mid-October.
items.title: Huawei Signals Price Hikes for Solar and Storage Gear

items.summary: A report from Georgetown and Duke researchers argues that batteries should be the first choice over gas plants for powering data centers, offering advice to states. The authors note developers are building more than 60 gigawatts of new utility-scale gas plants plus around 90 GW of behind-the-meter generators nationwide, a move they warn could cost money if computing demand fails and worsen climate change. Batteries, the report says, can hedge against stranded asset risk, are cheaper for short-term needs, and avoid costly grid buildouts. A BloombergNEF forecast cited in the piece projects U.S. energy storage deployment surpassing 11,000 gigawatt-hours by 2036, a 30% increase from its prior forecast.
items.title: Georgetown and Duke Report Recommends Batteries for Data Center Power

items.summary: A canceled $20 million EPA grant has left the Native Village of Kotzebue in northwest Alaska without a planned wind energy project, part of hundreds of millions removed from tribal communities by the Department of Government Efficiency. The tribe relies on diesel for 75% of its power and spends about 20% of income on it—more than three times the national low-income average. Two Brookings Institution reports argue that cuts to Inflation Reduction Act funding, including a $468 million DOGE reduction and canceled projects like Hopi Tribe solar grants totaling part of a $7 billion program, reflect long-standing underinvestment rather than isolated policy shifts. Authors call for legislation barring grant cancellations.
items.title: DOGE Cuts Leave Alaska Tribe Without Clean Energy Grant

items.summary: Blackstone rebranded its energy investment fund with the phrase “energy transition” in 2022 after already stopping oil and gas production investing. The fund raised $8.7 billion this year, reportedly turning away an additional $3 billion to stay under a cap. On Wall Street, the term covers natural gas plants, data centers, and rising electricity demand rather than only renewables. Analysts Dan Cohn of the Institute for Energy Economics and Financial Analysis and Ryan Loughead of BloombergNEF say investors see these as transition opportunities; some funds include methane despite Blackstone’s fund avoiding oil and gas fields. Critics argue gas is not a credible bridge fuel, and climate groups dispute its role.
items.title: Blackstone’s Energy Transition Fund Keeps Natural Gas and Data Centers in Focus

items.summary: Elia Transmission Belgium published results of three capacity remuneration mechanism auctions for the 2027-28, 2028-29 and 2030-31 delivery periods. Supply exceeded demand in all three rounds. Batteries formed a significant share of contracted capacity for 2028-29 and 2030-31, with four-hour batteries favored over two-hour units. The auctions totalled around €200 million ($223.7 million) for the first period to support Belgium’s security of supply amid its partial nuclear phaseout.
items.title: Belgium’s CRM Auctions Favor Batteries Across Three Delivery Periods

items.summary: An adviser to the European Union's highest court said on Tuesday that Google's AI chatbot Gemini may infringe copyright rules in certain circumstances. Advocate General Maciej Szpunar stated that reusing a press publisher's publication to generate an answer could violate rights, though copyrighted material used for training large language models remains freely permitted under the text and data mining exception.
items.title: EU Court Adviser Warns Google Gemini May Infringe Copyright Rules

items.summary: Reliance Industries' growth prospects are drawing renewed attention from its latest earnings and the listing of Jio Platforms. Analyst Deven Choksey of Dr Choksey Finserv Private Limited notes that strong refining margins, higher diesel cracks and discounted Venezuelan crude should support Reliance's Oil-to-Chemicals business, while Jio's valuation may unlock value for shareholders through potential dividends from its free cash flows. With EBITDA projected to rise from around ₹2.4–2.5 lakh crore to nearly ₹2.7 lakh crore, refining strength and the Jio valuation are cited as key growth triggers.
items.title: Three Catalysts Shape Reliance Industries Stock Outlook Amid Jio Listing and Refining Strength

items.summary: Mukesh Ambani overtook ByteDance founder Zhang Yiming to become Asia's richest person after a nearly 12% rise in Reliance Industries' stock added $8.5 billion to his wealth on Monday, per the item. His estimated net worth reached $88.8 billion according to Forbes' Real-Time Billionaires list, above Yiming's $84 billion.
items.title: Mukesh Ambani Surpasses Zhang Yiming as Asia's Richest Person After Reliance Stock Surge

items.summary: In Chile, returning ancestral land to Mapuche communities led them to replace commercial pine and eucalyptus plantations with grasslands for livestock, yet it produced no measurable gains in carbon storage or biodiversity. The authors examine the economic and environmental impacts of the Fund for Indigenous Land and Water (FTAI), which has returned more than 200,000 hectares to Indigenous control, mostly benefiting Mapuche communities. Restitution shifted land use toward grasslands with a reported 4.5% increase and an 18% decrease in plantation forests over time. However, restitution did not significantly improve carbon sequestration, biodiversity, or erosion control, nor change productivity as measured by the Enhanced Vegetation Index. The authors conclude that preventing initial dispossession may preserve ecosystem services more effectively than restoring heavily modified landscapes later (Jaimovich et al. 2026).
items.title: Chilean land returns empower Mapuche but miss ecological gains

items.summary: Virgin Media O2 announced thousands of UK job cuts as part of an £800m cost-cutting plan to address its £22bn debt. The company said up to a third of the workforce could be affected, with most losses coming from non-customer-facing roles while AI tools expand use across operations.
items.title: Virgin Media O2 Cuts Thousands of Jobs in Cost Drive

items.summary: European online fashion retailer Zalando launched its first AI shopping agent on Tuesday, amid concerns that artificial intelligence could disrupt online retail after reporting a third-quarter gross profit margin of 38.7 per cent below expectations. Shares fell 5 per cent in early trading. Analysts at Jefferies and JPMorgan cited investments as partly responsible for the shortfall.
items.title: Zalando Debuts AI Shopping Agent Amid Margin Pressure

items.summary: The authors link point-of-sale and payroll records at 20,000 U.S. firms to study tips. They find that tips are a nearly constant share of revenue, so hourly pay moves with it; when firms begin collecting tips they claw back between 23 and 33 cents per dollar through lower base wages. A calibrated model implies tipping raises job value by about half and firm profit by about 30 percent where customers tip readily.
items.title: Authors describe how tipping shifts worker pay with revenue

items.summary: November 3 is UNESCO's International Day for Biosphere Reserves, which combine biodiversity conservation, research and sustainable development. China hosts 36 reserves; its World Network now covers 797 sites across 145 countries spanning 7.5 million square kilometers, more than 5% of the Earth's terrestrial surface. The review at COP17 found the world remains off track to meet the Kunming-Montreal framework's targets for 2030.
items.title: Biosphere Reserves Link Conservation and Communities on UNESCO's International Day

items.summary: The Hukou Waterfall on the Yellow River, once shown as muddy and turbulent on China's fourth-series 50-yuan banknote, now presents clear cascading waters. Photographer Lyu Guiming noted that clear cascades have become his main photographic subject over the past decade. The change reflects decades of conservation efforts under Communist Party leadership since 1946. Yellow River Conservancy Commission figures show water quality improved markedly: the proportion of monitoring sections graded Class I to III rose from 59.1% in 2016 to 93.2% in 2025, according to YRCC.
items.title: Yellow River Runs Clearer After Decades of Conservation Efforts

items.summary: Chinese Premier Li Qiang met with Sultan Haitham Bin Tarik Al Said of Oman at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing on Monday, November 2, 2026. The two heads of state mapped out a blueprint for deepening their strategic partnership. Li said China is ready to deepen cooperation across oil and gas, clean energy projects, agriculture, aerospace satellites, information and communication, artificial intelligence, and cultural exchanges, while promoting free trade agreement negotiations with the Gulf Cooperation Council.
items.title: Chinese Premier Li Qiang Meets Sultan of Oman on State Visit

items.summary: As midterms approach, Americans cite cost of living as their top concern amid soaring food and fuel prices linked to tariffs and the Iran war. Diesel hit a record $6.52 in September from $3.75 before February, while inflation rose to 3.7% from 3%. Trump's approval has fallen but final polls put it around 38%, with only 29% viewing Democrats positively—suggesting anger may not shift votes. Republicans face defensive races in the heartland; Democrats expect House gains and watch for lessons before 2028, though polls historically overstate Democratic support.
items.title: Midterm Voters Weigh Trump's War and Soaring Prices

items.summary: Virgin Media O2 plans to cut thousands of jobs as part of an £800m cost-cutting drive while tackling its £22bn debt. The company, jointly owned by Liberty Global and Telefónica, said £300m of savings would come from job cuts reducing the wage bill 30% over two years, possibly affecting up to 25% of its 16,000 workforce. Chief executive Lutz Schüler framed the moves as necessary for future growth.
items.title: Virgin Media O2 Announces Thousands of Job Cuts Amid £800m Cost Drive

items.summary: The dictionary publisher Collins has named “mogging” its word of the year for 2026, according to copywriter Rachel Quin. The term describes outperforming or making someone look inferior in appearance, confidence or status. Quin said it originated around 2016 in bodybuilding culture before entering everyday slang by 2026.
items.title: Collins Names Mogging Its Word of the Year

items.summary: CD Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel Alameda, aged 30, died after suffering head and chest injuries in a collision with Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono during a second-division match. His condition was described as stable but serious on Monday before worsening neurologically; Spanish media reported cardiac arrest en route to hospital. He passed away at 07:00 GMT (08:00 local time). The club and co-owned opponent Andorra issued statements of condolence, with the family requesting privacy.
items.title: Tenerife Striker Jesus de Miguel Dies After On-Field Collision

items.summary: West Ham United ended Nuno Espirito Santo's tenure on Tuesday after back-to-back defeats left them eighth in the Championship while pursuing a Premier League return. He joined the struggling club in September 2025, but could not prevent relegation to the second tier for the first time since 2011. The Board of Directors said a change was necessary as recruiting a new head coach is already underway.
items.title: West Ham dismiss Nuno Espirito Santo as manager

items.summary: Ayu Yoneda, Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency's youngest astronaut at 31, says she wants to broadcast from the moon in Japanese. For decades every lunar transmission has been spoken only in English since Neil Armstrong landed there in 1969. In an interview with The Japan Times, Yoneda said she hopes her words will connect people back home and anyone learning our language.
items.title: Japan's Youngest Astronaut Wants to Speak Japanese on the Moon

items.summary: The United States imposed new sanctions on Rwanda's Ministry of Defense over its role in the conflict in the Democratic Republic of Congo, following earlier measures against Burundi and the Rwandan army announced on 2 mars 2026. The U.S. State Department justifies these steps by Washington agreements signed on 4 décembre 2025 aimed at ending the war. A doctoral researcher analyzing international sanctions argues the penalties target only Rwanda despite mutual violations, noting academic estimates of their success rate range from about 34 % to roughly 4 %, according to Robert Anthony Pape. The article warns such one-sided pressure may undermine diplomatic credibility and backfire in a region where power dynamics prevail.
items.title: U.S. Sanctions on Rwanda Draw Criticism Over Selectivity

items.summary: China's top diplomat Wang Yi held talks with Musaad bin Mohammed Al-Aiban, Saudi Arabia's Minister of State and National Security Advisor, in Beijing on Monday. Al-Aiban handed over a letter from Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman to Chinese President Xi Jinping on bilateral relations. Wang said China places its ties with Saudi Arabia among its Middle East diplomatic priorities.
items.title: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi Holds Talks With Saudi National Security Advisor In Beijing.

items.summary: CD Tenerife announced that striker Jesús de Miguel Alameda died on November 3, 2026. He was struck in the chest by Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono during a second division match tied 2-2 at Estadio Heliodoro Rodríguez López. De Miguel, then 30 years old, had been taken to Hospital Universitario de Nuestra Señora de Candelaria.
items.title: Tenerife Striker Jesús de Miguel Dies After Match Collision

items.summary: Indian farmer Amarsingh Gushinge, 78, plans to sow wheat and chickpeas but cannot plant either crop because dwindling water supplies follow below-average monsoon rains. Like him, millions of farmers in southern and western India face shortages as they prepare winter crops. The Jalna district around his village received about 48% less rain than average this year, the local weather office has said.
items.title: Weak Monsoon Threatens Winter Crops Across India

items.summary: Todd Russell, a Beaconsfield mine collapse survivor who was trapped underground in 2006 and later received an undisclosed illness diagnosis announced in July 2024, has said he is leaving hospital treatment. He posted that after years of pain, uncertainty and treatments he now feels there are no further options medically or physically, and will see out his days at home surrounded by family.
items.title: Beaconsfield survivor Todd Russell leaves hospital amid health battle

items.summary: Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt's daughter Vivienne has legally changed her surname, becoming known as Vivienne Jolie after filing paperwork in Los Angeles County Superior Court on 12 July. She is the fifth of their six children to drop 'Jolie-Pitt,' following Shiloh, Maddox and Zahara; Pax remains the only child still using the double-barreled name. The split dates from a 2016 airplane altercation in which Pitt allegedly became verbally abusive and physical with one of his kids, though an FBI investigation cleared him of all charges.
items.title: Vivienne Jolie Drops Pitt From Her Surname

items.summary: A BizDataDive piece frames China's digital economy as accelerating, tied to the ongoing 2026 World Internet Conference held in Wuzhen, Zhejiang Province. The article points to rising digital consumption and breakthroughs in technology and innovation as signs of broad-based momentum building across sectors. It invites readers to examine these developments through supporting figures.
items.title: China's digital economy gains momentum at Wuzhen Summit

items.summary: Work on a luxury resort inside Zanzibar's Ngezi-Vumawimbi Forest Reserve appears to have halted after contractors built a boundary wall in the first half of 2026. Details remain opaque, and conservationists published an open letter opposing the Mantuli project over threats to endemic species. Ecologist Tim Caro said it could affect nearly a quarter of mature trees; botanists warned of possible orchid extinctions. Surrounding communities rely on forest resources for income. Mongabay contacted ZIPA but received no response.
items.title: Construction stalls at Zanzibar forest resort amid biodiversity concerns

items.summary: The Gaza Strip’s Education Ministry said at least 14 school students and eight education workers were killed in Israeli attacks on the enclave in October, according to a statement published late Monday. Victims included children aged between 6 and 16, teachers, university staff and an academic struck in a residential apartment. The ministry also reported class disruptions across southern Khan Younis, eastern Deir al-Balah, the Bureij refugee camp and northern Gaza Strip areas.
items.title: Gaza Education Ministry Reports October Killings of Students and Teachers

items.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tuesday that Tehran continues dialogue with Saudi Arabia while seeking regional security arrangements led by regional countries and away from foreign military presence. He praised Qatar’s mediation, outlined a Qatari-mediated plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz after US measures, and denied reports of an agreement for direct talks. The remarks come amid indirect contacts between Iran and Washington following the Feb. 28 war.
items.title: Iran Says Talks With Saudi Arabia Continue Amid Hormuz Proposal

items.summary: Ethiopian authorities indefinitely suspended the licence of independent newspaper The Reporter on Monday, November 2, 2026, saying it published content that contradicts national interests. The Ethiopian Media Authority (EMA) said the outlet was ordered to remain fully suspended until legal and ethical obligations are met, citing reports that negatively affect foreign investment, tourism and diplomacy. This is part of a broader restriction on press freedom in Ethiopia.
items.title: Ethiopia Suspends Independent Newspaper The Reporter

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India relaxed Export Declaration Form compliance for resident individuals exporting services, per a November 2 notification. Such exporters need only supply payment-related information to their authorised dealer bank instead of filing an EDF separately. The amendment applies retrospectively from October 1, 2026. Non-individual exporters may use simplified reporting for inward remittances up to ₹10 lakh per transaction.
items.title: RBI Relaxes EDF Compliance for Individual Service Exporters

items.summary: Google has launched Dreambeans, an experimental app available through Google Labs for users aged 18 and above. The app turns details from a user's connected daily activity into personalised illustrated stories overnight, aiming to replace endless social feeds with content that reflects what matters to each person. Stories can cover topics worth exploring, places to visit, arts and crafts activities, things to try and event reminders, built using Google Photos and Nano Banana 2 artwork.
items.title: Google Launches Dreambeans AI App in India

items.summary: Reliance Industries Chairman Mukesh Ambani overtook ByteDance co-founder Zhang Yiming to become Asia's richest person, per Forbes' Real-Time Billionaires list on Tuesday. His estimated wealth rose 10.5% to $88.8 billion, ranking him 22nd globally. The gain followed a nearly 12% surge in Reliance shares that added more than $19 billion to market capitalisation. Reliance reported its strongest quarterly performance for July-September, with revenue up 28% and net profit climbing 34% to Rs29,550 crore.
items.title: Mukesh Ambani Surpasses Zhang Yiming as Asia's Richest Individual

items.summary: Srinagar Lok Sabha member Aga Syed Ruhullah Mehdi resigned from Parliament and the National Conference on Tuesday, marking a setback for the ruling party. News agency PTI reported he hinted at forming a new party of "honest and compassionate people." His resignation follows growing discontent within NC, with about 25 legislators reportedly demanding replacement of all eight cabinet ministers within 15 days.
items.title: NC MP Resigns Amid Party Revolt

items.summary: KRBL shares rose roughly 9% after second-quarter net profit jumped about 51% year-on-year to Rs 259 crore from Rs 172 crore. Consolidated revenue climbed around 14% YoY to Rs 1,727.4 crore in Q2FY27 versus Rs 1,511.1 crore a year earlier, driven mainly by higher domestic sales that partly offset weaker exports.
items.title: KRBL Shares Rally on Strong Q2 Profit Jump

items.summary: Trident reported Q2 net profit of Rs 175 crore, up 93% year-on-year. EBITDA rose 46.5% to Rs 313.7 crore while revenue fell 4%. The towel segment declined as yarn grew. Trident plans a new yarn facility in Dhar with capacity for 1,99,680 spindles and an 80-megawatt renewable energy project.
items.title: Trident shares rally on profit jump and capex plans

items.summary: The BJP targeted All India Students' Association (AISA) president Neha Bora on Tuesday after a video surfaced showing her criticising the Brahmanical system. Spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari shared it, calling her Rahul Gandhi's 'poster girl' and accusing her of spreading Hindu hate. The remarks came amid protests against election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over electoral roll irregularities. The undated video could not be independently verified.
items.title: BJP targets AISA president Neha Bora over Hindu remarks

items.summary: The Indian government issued draft rules on September 30, 2026, open for public comment until November 5, 2026. They would let institutional ethics committees approve mild and moderate animal experiments without central approval from the CCSEA, which currently handles most cases above rodents. Critics including PETA India called them backward and said they could significantly weaken protections, citing a conflict of interest since five of nine committee members come from the approving institute, plus subjective severity categories. The draft also permits wild, stray animals and livestock from open markets. Animal rights groups argue lab-bred animals are needed for reliable data. As context, more than 2,300 facilities were registered with the CCSEA as of 2022, and a Grand View Research report estimated the CRO preclinical animal-trial market at $183.3 million in 2023, growing about 11.4% annually through 2030.
items.title: Draft India Rules Would Let Local Committees Approve Mild and Moderate Animal Tests

items.summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh said India aims for defence production of Rs 3 lakh crore and exports worth Rs 50,000 crore by 2029. He noted production rose from Rs 46,429 crore in 2014-15 to a record Rs 1.78 lakh crore in 2025-26, while exports grew from under Rs 2,000 crore to about Rs 40,000 crore. Singh stressed strategic autonomy and indigenous capability at the Jaisalmer Consultative Committee meeting.
items.title: India Targets Record Defence Production and Exports by 2029

items.summary: The Bombay High Court said it was "disturbed" by politicians targeting actor Dia Mirza over a video she shot for the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation urging residents not to light firecrackers on public streets during Diwali. The court directed BMC to re-upload the clip and called objections communal, noting India is secular and festivals belong to everyone.
items.title: HC ‘disturbed’ by politicians’ comments targeting Dia Mirza Diwali video, orders BMC to re-upload it

items.summary: The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation removed a video of actor Dia Mirza urging Mumbai residents not to light firecrackers during Diwali, following objections from the Bharatiya Janata Party. The BJP’s Mumbai unit chief Ameet Satam said “We don’t need lessons on how to celebrate Diwali from Dia Mirza.” BMC did not state why it deleted the clip; Mayor Ritu Tawde called Mirza an anti-Hindu and anti-government figure who would be blacklisted.
items.title: BMC Deletes Dia Mirza Diwali Video After BJP Objection

items.summary: Tukaram Mundhe, Maharashtra FDA Commissioner, broke a laddu at a Pune event to inspect its quality before Diwali. The gesture drew praise from social media users as an honest officer. Separately, the FDA seized about 1,190 kg of goods worth around ₹1.73 lakh in Kondhwa after finding excessive food colouring and poor hygiene.
items.title: Maharashtra FDA Commissioner's Laddu Inspection Goes Viral Amid Diwali Food Safety Push

items.summary: Gordon Ramsay and his wife Tana have reportedly bought a second property on the same street as their existing Rock home, in what would be the most expensive house ever sold in Cornwall at £9.65 million. The report comes from the Evening Standard, which said it had contacted Ramsay’s representative for comment, so details remain unconfirmed. If accurate, the 19th-century four-bedroom property with a two-acre plot surpasses their earlier £7.5 million purchase of Daymer Bay House in 2022. The story reflects wider tensions over high-end second-home ownership and its effect on local communities.
items.title: Ramsay reportedly buys second Cornwall home for £9.65 million

items.summary: University of Washington researchers created a computer simulation modelling Earth over roughly five billion years, from formation around 4.5 billion years ago extending about 500 million years into the future, deliberately excluding biological activity to establish how natural geological and atmospheric processes alone shape planetary conditions. Published in The Planetary Science Journal on September 18, 2026, and announced by the university on November 2, the model reproduced 19 key observations of pre-industrial Earth within estimated measurement uncertainties. Lead author Samantha Gilbert-Janizek says it may help distinguish non-biological from biological atmospheric signals; senior author Rory Barnes calls it an important step toward more reliable simulations for studying distant worlds.
items.title: Washington model simulates lifeless Earth for exoplanet study

items.summary: The Bharatiya Janata Party is organising a full-day Sikh conclave in Chandigarh on 4 November to address the 1984 anti-Sikh riots and seek justice for victims' families. The event features victim families, legal experts, retired Justice S.N. Dhingra, former Union Minister Ravi Shankar Prasad, Advocate H.S. Phoolka, and Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini, with party leader R.P. Singh coordinating preparations.
items.title: Gujarat ATS Takes Custody Of Drug Kingpin Salim Dola After Turkey Deportation

items.summary: The Bharatiya Janata Party is organising a full-day Sikh conclave in Chandigarh on 4 November to address the 1984 anti-Sikh riots and seek justice for victims' families. The event will feature victim families, legal experts and senior leaders, including former Union Minister Ravi Shankar Prasad and Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini. An exhibition will cover the violence's history and government investigative measures. The initiative aims to strengthen BJP presence in Punjab ahead of state elections.
items.title: BJP Launches Sikh Conclave in Chandigarh on Anti-Riots Justice Push

items.summary: SBI Research, in its ECOWRAP report dated November 2, pitches abolishing long-term capital gains tax on equities and raising securities transaction tax to offset revenue loss. It also proposes expanding the savings deposit exemption from Rs 10,000 to Rs 20,000 (foregone revenue around Rs 1,531 crore) and a flat 15 per cent rate for term deposits (around Rs 10,500 crore), totalling about Rs 12,000 crore. The proposals follow an estimate that the Centre's FY27 fiscal deficit could exceed the Budget Estimate by around Rs 1.2 lakh crore.
items.title: SBI Research Proposes Abolishing LTCG Tax Amid Fiscal Deficit Concerns

items.summary: An 11-year-old boy in class 4 died after touching a high-tension electricity wire on the rooftop of a government primary school in Ballia district, Uttar Pradesh. Officials said he came into contact with the line and died shortly afterward. The family alleged that a teacher sent him to pluck a gourd from the terrace. Locals protested; police registered an FIR against a suspect, suspended two staff members, terminated one teacher's service, and sent the body for post-mortem examination.
items.title: Uttar Pradesh Boy Dies After Contact With High-Tension Line at School

items.summary: Chief Minister V D Satheesan said on Tuesday that no legislature can reject a Comptroller and Auditor General report, calling the January 2021 Kerala Assembly resolution excluding KIOCL audit findings an unhealthy practice. He argued such moves defeat parliamentary accountability. He also criticised CAG methodology for overstating losses in the 2G spectrum allocation as ₹1.76 lakh crore and misjudging Vizhinjam port. Satheesan urged a discussion on how Public Accounts Committees should treat out-of-scope audit findings and called for clearing files pending over 20 years.
items.title: Kerala CM Challenges CAG Audit Authority Over Parliament Reports

items.summary: The Indian Navy rescued all 20 crew members of the fishing vessel Azini from Somali pirates in a Monday operation off Somalia's coast. The Iranian Embassy thanked India, its Navy and Air Force for the swift rescue. In 2026 so far, Somali pirates have hijacked at least 8 vessels amid around 15 attacks or seizures, the highest since 2013.
items.title: Indian Navy Rescues Iranian Crew From Somali Pirates

items.summary: Garment workers in Bangladesh are protesting and prompting factory shutdowns as they demand more than double the current minimum wage, Tk 30,000 a month (about $245), versus the present Tk 12,500. More than 500 factories have closed, leaving nearly one million workers without work. Workers cite rising living costs for food, housing, transport and healthcare. The government formed a wage board to review pay, but factory owners say the increase is financially unfeasible.
items.title: Bangladesh Garment Workers Demand Wage Hike Amid Protests

items.summary: Natural rubber in India crossed Rs 300 a kg for the first time, per prices released by the Rubber Board, which listed RSS-4 (Grade One) at Rs 300 and latex with 60 per cent Dry Rubber Content at Rs 197.60. The board chairman called it a historic high that fulfils farmers' long-standing expectations. Yet growers say rising cultivation costs, a shortage of skilled tappers and declining yields keep eroding earnings; Tony P Emmanuel said yield from an acre has fallen to nearly one-third of its level 15 years ago, and warned the sector would stay in crisis even at Rs 500 per kg. Latex processor Martin Joseph reported losses of around Rs 80 lakh over four months as raw-material costs outstrip selling prices.
items.title: Kerala Rubber Prices Hit Record High Amid Cost Pressures
